chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār from 'Abd Ṣāliḥ (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had a female servant, and she bore a girl. His servant breastfed his son, and the mother of his child (the concubine) breastfed the servant's daughter. Thus, the man became the father of the servant's daughter through breastfeeding. [I asked if] he sells her? He said: 'Yes, if he wishes, he sells her and benefits from her price.' I said: 'But if he had gifted her to some of his family when she was born, and his son is today a young man, does he sell her and take her price without consulting his son, or does his son sell her?' He said: 'He sells her, and his son takes the price, and the son's wealth is for him [the father].' I said: 'Does he sell the servant, who has breastfed his son?' He said: 'Yes, and I like for him not to sell her.' I said: 'But if he needs her price?' He said: 'Then he sells her.'

His saying (peace be upon him) in the beginning of the report: 'If he wishes, he sells her and benefits from her price' refers to the breastfeeding servant, not her daughter. Do you not see that he clarified this at the end of the report when the questioner said to him: 'Does he sell the servant, who has breastfed his son?' [The Imam responded with] surprise at that by his saying (peace be upon him): 'Yes,' and although it is disliked, except in case of need, according to what we have previously mentioned from his saying (peace be upon him): 'And I like for him not to sell her.' And if the servant were the mother of his child by lineage, it would be permissible for him to sell her, according to what we have previously mentioned.

key_terms.أَبُو الْبِنْتِ مِنَ الرَّضَاعِ: Father of the daughter through breastfeeding
key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (concubine who bore her master's child)
key_terms.الرَّضَاعُ: Breastfeeding (used here to establish kinship/milk relationship)
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: Disliked (a legal ruling between permissible and forbidden)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master selling a female servant who breastfed his son?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between *umm al-walad* (mother of the child) and a concubine who breastfeeds, affirming the master's right to sell the latter and retain the proceeds despite the breastfeeding bond. It further resolves the ownership of the servant's daughter, establishing that the master may sell her even if gifted to the family, while noting that selling the breastfeeding servant is disliked (*makruh*) unless necessitated by financial need. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the primacy of ownership rights over secondary familial bonds in the context of slavery.
